userStories.title: Add the bot-fix-chain advisor kind, menu and disabled caller switch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give the existing advisor a bot-fix-chain question kind, a three-option menu and an opt-in caller switch.

**Motivation** — What is missing is a decision point between the review and the fixer.

**Approach** — `packages/nax/src/config/schemas-advisor.ts`, `callers`.
Baseline: `{ finishJudgment, fixCycleGiveUp, uncategorisedFailure, finishApproval }`, each `z.boolean().default(false)`.
Target: the same four plus `botFixChain: z.boolean().default(false)`. `AdvisorCallersConfig` in `runtime-types-advisor.ts` gains `botFixChain: boolean`.

`packages/nax/src/advisor/types.ts`, `AdviceQuestionKind` and `MenuFacts`.
Baseline: seven kinds, ending in `"residual"`.
Target: the same plus `"bot-fix-chain"`, and `MenuFacts` gains the member `{ kind: "bot-fix-chain" }`.

`packages/nax/src/advisor/menus.ts`, `buildMenu(facts: MenuFacts): AdviceOption[]`.
Target: for `{ kind: "bot-fix-chain" }` it returns exactly three options, in this order: type `fix`, type `waive`, type `hold`, with ids assigned by the existing `withIds`.

Adds `advisor.callers.botFixChain` (default `false`) to the schema, the runtime type and the config description table. Adds the question kind `"bot-fix-chain"`, its `MenuFacts` member and its three-option menu.

`packages/nax/test/unit/config/advisor-config.test.ts` — two assertions pin `advisor.callers` with `toEqual` on exactly four keys (the defaults test and "a partial block keeps the other defaults"). Both gain `botFixChain: false`; the invariant that replaces them is that every caller, `botFixChain` included, defaults to `false` and an unnamed caller keeps its default. Extend the existing menu tests and reuse validateAdvisorReply rather than adding bot-specific validation.

**Scope** — In: schema/runtime type, config description, kind/menu, corresponding unit behavior. Out: routing selection (US-004), evidence (US-005), advisor calls (US-006). Turning the caller on by default: `advisor.callers.botFixChain` defaults to `false`. Changing what `needsHumanConfirm` means, when the advisor service sets it, or the severity set `forcedConfirm` reads. Documentation outside the config description table: the bot guide is updated by hand after the feature lands.

**Interface** — `botFixChain: z.boolean().default(false)`; `AdvisorCallersConfig` gains `botFixChain: boolean`; `AdviceQuestionKind` gains `"bot-fix-chain"`; `MenuFacts` gains `{ kind: "bot-fix-chain" }`; `buildMenu(facts: MenuFacts): AdviceOption[]` retains its signature.

userStories.title: Apply advisor waives through the existing finding settlement rule
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let an own advisor waived comment settle a finding with newest-writer precedence and no redundant echo.

**Motivation** — The loop ended only when a human read the base branch, the spec's Out of Scope and the README, restored the lines to the base behaviour, and waived the root finding.

**Approach** — **An advisor waive settles the finding the way a writer's waive does (US-003).** `latestFindingRuling` is the one place that decides which reply rules a finding thread. It gains one case: an own comment whose marker key starts with `cr-` and whose body `parseChainRuling` reads as outcome `waived` is a ruling with disposition `waived`. Scanning stays newest-first, so a writer's later reply (`confirm`, `waive:`, `override:`) outranks the advisor, and the advisor's comment outranks any older writer reply. Every reader that goes through `latestFindingRuling` follows with no further change: `recordFindingRulings`, `readSettledKeys`, `readConfirmedKeys`.

`packages/nax/src/bot/finding-rulings.ts`, `latestFindingRuling(input, thread): Promise<FindingRulingCandidate | null>`.
Baseline: skips every own comment; returns the newest non-own reply that parses as a ruling keyword and whose author may rule.
Target: same signature. Scanning newest-first, an own comment whose marker key starts with `cr-` and for which `parseChainRuling` returns outcome `waived` is returned as a candidate with `keyword: { disposition: "waived", reason: <the ruling text> }`, that comment as `reply`, and its index. Every other own comment is still skipped. `isWriter` is not called for it.

`packages/nax/src/bot/finding-rulings.ts`, the private `recordThread`.
Target: when the candidate's reply is an own chain ruling comment, no echo is posted for it (the comment is the record); the thread is still resolved when it is not already.

A comment counts as a chain ruling only when all three hold: it is an own comment (`ownComments`), its marker key starts with `cr-`, and `parseChainRuling` reads its body.

Each AC builds the thread with a first comment by the bot carrying the finding marker key `f-1`. "An own chain ruling" is a comment by the bot wrapped with `withNaxBotMarker(renderChainRuling(ruling), chainRulingKey("f-1"))`. Use existing finding-rulings.test.ts and rulings.test.ts for recorder and reader assertions. Authorization failures must continue to deny only that reply.

**Scope** — In: latestFindingRuling and recordThread changes, existing recorder and settlement-reader behavior. Out: creating/posting routing rulings (US-006), replay/parent/confirmation routing (US-007), chain grammar changes (US-002), rewriting settlement logic in each reader.

**Interface** — `latestFindingRuling(input, thread): Promise<FindingRulingCandidate | null>` keeps its existing arguments and result shape; `recordFindingRulings`, `readSettledKeys` and `readConfirmedKeys` keep their interfaces.

userStories.title: Build one chain question with finding, ledger and git evidence
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build the complete advisor draft for one chain finding using existing lineage and checkout inputs.

**Motivation** — Every step of that human ruling used inputs the bot already has at fix time: the finding, its lineage, the push ledger, and the checkout.

**Approach** — **The question** (`buildChainQuestion`):

- `kind: "bot-fix-chain"`, `feature`: the given feature, `options: buildMenu({ kind: "bot-fix-chain" })`, `findingSeverity`: the finding's severity, `anchorFile`: the finding's file when it has one, `rulingTitle`: the first line of the finding's issue, `dedupeKey`: the chain ruling key.
- `summary`: exactly `Finding <key> (<severity>) sits at generation <n> on lines nax bot fix <first seven characters of the push sha> added.`
- `evidence`, in this order:
  1. `source: "finding"`: the issue, `file:line`, severity, trigger and trigger evidence, origin and origin evidence, and the reviewer's suggestion.
  2. `source: "review-round"`: one entry for the lineage push, listing each parent key with the issue the ledger recorded for it (`parentIssue` over `ownLedgerEntries(env.own)`), or the key alone when the ledger no longer holds it.
  3. `source: "diff"`, `ref: <file>`: the standard output of `git diff <env.checkout.mergeBase>..HEAD -- <file>` run in `env.checkout.worktree`, when the finding has a file.
  4. `source: "diff"`, `ref: <pushSha>`: the standard output of `git show <pushSha> -- <file>`, when the finding has a file.
- A diff text longer than `CHAIN_DIFF_CHARS` is cut to its first `CHAIN_DIFF_CHARS` characters and followed by a newline and the line `(diff cut at 12000 characters)`.
- A git command that exits non-zero, times out or rejects leaves its evidence entry out; the draft is still returned.

**Files.** The question builder lives in its own file, `chain-question.ts`, so that `chain-advise.ts` stays well under the 600-line source limit.

A ledger entry is read only when its `sha` is 40 lowercase hex characters (`FULL_SHA` in `push-ledger.ts`). Every AC uses a routed env and a chain finding as defined in US-004, with key `f-1`, severity `important`, file `src/a.ts`, line 12, a suggestion, and lineage `{ generation: 2, pushSha: "abcdef1000000000000000000000000000000000", parents: ["f-p1", "f-p2"] }`. env.own holds an own push ledger entry for that full sha, with f-p1's issue `first parent issue` and no f-p2. Stub _chainQuestionDeps.runGit in every test.

**Scope** — In: chain-question.ts, question metadata/evidence, diff caps and independent git failure fallback, chain-question.test.ts. Out: deciding an outcome, creating an advisor or posting (US-006), replay (US-007), changing the menu (US-001). Supplying the PRD text to the advisor when the feature directory is absent from the main checkout: the advisor prompt carries `{}` there.

**Interface**
```ts
export const _chainQuestionDeps = { runGit: botGit };
export const CHAIN_DIFF_CHARS = 12_000;
export function buildChainQuestion(env: BotFixEnv, finding: ChainFinding, feature: string): Promise<QuestionDraft>;
```
Wire the actual builder into _chainAdviseDeps once this module exists; US-006 consumes the exact draft it returns.

userStories.title: Ask the advisor and durably apply each chain outcome
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Transform a routed fix environment by asking once per own-thread chain finding and committing outcomes through thread replies.

**Motivation** — A prompt-only rule cannot close this gap.

**Approach** — `withChainRulings` asks the advisor one question per chain finding, maps each decision to an outcome (`fix`, `waived`, `held` or `unruled`), posts the outcome on the finding's thread, and returns the environment the fix graph runs on (US-006).

**The returned environment.** Waived and held items are removed from `review.agreed`. A `fix` item and an `unruled` item stay, unchanged and in place. `env.chainRulings` lists one `ChainRuling` per finding that has a `fix` or `held` outcome in this run, and per finding the advisor waived in this run, in `review.agreed` order. That includes an outcome replayed from an existing comment (composition test 4) and a hold made without asking (tests 4 and 5). An `unruled` finding has no entry, and neither has a finding removed because its thread already carries a `waived` chain ruling. `AgreedItem` is not changed: the instruction travels in `chainRulings`, and `chainInstructions(env)` gives the fix step a map from finding key to instruction. Replay and no-second-call behavior are US-007; chainInstructions and fix consumers are US-008.

**The advisor call** (`withChainRulings`): one advisor is created per call, with `callCtx: env.ctx.callCtx`, `repoRoot: env.repoRoot`, `outputDir` and `runId` from `env.ctx.callCtx.runtime`, `feature` and `specPath` from `chainRoutingContext`, `workdir: env.checkout.worktree`. Each finding is asked with `advise(draft, { findingSeverity: item.severity })`, inside `env.ctx.sessionScope` when it is present.

The advisor prompt carries the feature's PRD text as read from the main checkout; for a feature that exists only on the pull request's branch that text is `{}`. The question's own evidence is what the ruling rests on.

**The advisor session is base-pinned like the fix session.** When `env.ctx.sessionScope` is present, each `advise` call runs inside it, so the advisor session does not load agent configuration files from the pull request's head. `branch-fix.ts` applies the same scope to the fix session.

**Decision to outcome.**
| Decision | Outcome | `text` | `proposed` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `null` | `unruled` | | |
| action `fix`, `needsHumanConfirm` false | `fix` | `action.instruction` | |
| action `waive`, `needsHumanConfirm` false | `waived` | `action.reason` | |
| action `hold` | `held` | `action.reason` | |
| action `fix`, `needsHumanConfirm` true | `held` | `decision.rationale` | `{ outcome: "fix", text: action.instruction }` |
| action `waive`, `needsHumanConfirm` true | `held` | `decision.rationale` | `{ outcome: "waived", text: action.reason }` |
| any other action type | `unruled` | | |

**Posting.** For `fix`, `waived` and `held` the routing replies on the finding's own thread with `withNaxBotMarker(renderChainRuling(ruling), chainRulingKey(item.key))`, then resolves the thread for `waived`. The `ChainRuling` recorded in `env.chainRulings` carries the text as posted, that is, the text `parseChainRuling` would read back.

**Outcome `unruled` is today's behaviour.** The item stays in `review.agreed` unchanged, no `ChainRuling` is recorded for it, and no comment is kept as its ruling. It is the result when the item has no own thread, when the cost limit is reached, when the advisor returns no decision or `advise` rejects, and when posting the ruling comment fails, whatever the outcome would have been. The cost limit test is delivered in US-007.

Composition tests delivered here: 3. The item has no own thread: outcome `unruled`. The advisor is not asked. 7. Otherwise the advisor is asked. Tests 2, 4, 5 and 6 are US-007's code: US-006 delivers tests 3 and 7 and asks the advisor about every chain finding that has an own thread. Gate using chainRoutingContext and selectChainFindings first; disabled/inapplicable/empty selection returns the same env with no ruling read or advisor creation.

Failure handling: decision null leaves work unchanged and logs a warning with key/fallbackReason; rejected advise leaves that item unruled but continues to later items; unsupported action is unruled. Failed reply is unruled regardless of proposed outcome, with no record or resolution. Failed resolution after a posted waive leaves the ruling standing and logs a warning. Warnings carry item keys; their text is not pinned. No input environment mutation.

**Scope** — In: withChainRulings, optional BotFixEnv.chainRulings, decision mapping, session scope, posting and failure fallback; use chain-advise-outcomes.test.ts. Out: confirmed-key reading, replay, parent holds and cost tests (US-007), prompt/summary/run wiring (US-008), readiness (US-009). Batching several chain findings into one advisor call (`adviseBatch`): one question per finding. A dedicated model key for this caller: the advisor's own `advisor.model` and `advisor.fallbackModels` apply. Choosing a model different from the reviewer's and fixer's is the operator's config, not enforced. Changing what `needsHumanConfirm` means, when the advisor service sets it, or the severity set `forcedConfirm` reads. Any change to `BOT_FIX_GRAPH`: no node, exit, transition or `BotFixState` field is added. Any change to `packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts` or to the `AgreedItem` type: the instruction travels in `BotFixEnv.chainRulings`.

**Interface**
```ts
export const _chainAdviseDeps = { createAdvisor, buildChainQuestion, readConfirmedKeys, replyToThread, resolveThread, getLogger };
export function withChainRulings(env: BotFixEnv): Promise<BotFixEnv>;
// BotFixEnv gains:
readonly chainRulings?: readonly ChainRuling[];
```
The existing service interface remains `createAdvisor(actx: AdvisorCallContext): Advisor`, `Advisor.advise(question: QuestionDraft, opts?: { findingSeverity?: string }): Promise<AdviceResult>`. The service checks neither enabled nor caller flags; the routing owns these gates. The draft severity alone does not feed forcedConfirm, so always supply opts.findingSeverity too. Unit setup: routed makeBotFixEnv with own-thread f-1, suggestion and important severity; stub createAdvisor, buildChainQuestion, replyToThread, resolveThread, and readConfirmedKeys (empty set, not asserted here). Default advise result is fix/restore the guard/no confirmation; cost stays below its limit.

userStories.title: Replay rulings, honor writers and hold repeated ruled chains
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce the ordered composition that prevents a second advisor ruling while respecting writer confirmation and the run budget.

**Motivation** — Rounds 1 and 4 raised the same finding.

**Approach** — **Composition.** For each agreed item, in `review.agreed` order, these tests apply in this order. The first that matches decides, and later tests are not evaluated for that item:

1. Not a finding, or `isBlockingFinding(item, blocking)` is false, or `item.lineage` is absent, or `item.lineage.generation` is below the configured notice generation: not a chain finding. The item stays unchanged. (US-004)
2. The item's key is in the confirmed keys (`readConfirmedKeys`): a writer has ruled that the work stands. The item stays unchanged and the advisor is not asked. (US-007)
3. The item has no own thread: outcome `unruled`. The advisor is not asked. (US-006)
4. The item's own thread already carries a chain ruling comment (US-007). The newest one decides, and the advisor is not asked:
   - outcome `held`: the item is removed, the hold is recorded in `chainRulings` with the comment's text, and nothing is posted;
   - outcome `waived`: the item is removed and nothing is posted;
   - outcome `fix`, and no own comment with marker key `fix-<item key>` comes after it on the thread: the item stays, with the recorded text as its instruction, and nothing is posted;
   - outcome `fix`, and an own `fix-<item key>` comment comes after it: outcome `held` with the text `raised again after an advisor-ruled fix`, posted as a new chain ruling comment.
5. One of `item.lineage.parents` has a chain ruling: an own comment anywhere on the pull request whose marker key is `chainRulingKey(parent)`, or a ruling this same call already made for that parent key. Outcome `held` with the text `a second finding on this chain`; the advisor is not asked. (US-007)
6. `env.cost.spentUsd() >= env.cost.limitUsd`: outcome `unruled` for this item and for every later item that reaches this test. (US-007)
7. Otherwise the advisor is asked. (US-006)

Test 2 precedes test 4 so that a writer's `confirm` on a held thread releases the item. Test 4 precedes test 5 so that a finding ruled once is not re-held by its own ancestry. Tests 2, 4, 5 and 6 are US-007's code: US-006 delivers tests 3 and 7 and asks the advisor about every chain finding that has an own thread.

A comment counts as a chain ruling only when all three hold: it is an own comment (`ownComments`), its marker key starts with `cr-`, and `parseChainRuling` reads its body.

**The returned environment.** Waived and held items are removed from `review.agreed`. A `fix` item and an `unruled` item stay, unchanged and in place. `env.chainRulings` lists one `ChainRuling` per finding that has a `fix` or `held` outcome in this run, and per finding the advisor waived in this run, in `review.agreed` order. That includes an outcome replayed from an existing comment (composition test 4) and a hold made without asking (tests 4 and 5). An `unruled` finding has no entry, and neither has a finding removed because its thread already carries a `waived` chain ruling.

Failure handling: `readConfirmedKeys` rejects — `withChainRulings` rejects with the same error; no item is sent to a fixer on a ruling that could not be read (same rule as `withCarriedFixFindings`). A comment with a `cr-` marker key does not parse — it is not a chain ruling: composition tests 4 and 5 do not match on it. The cost-limit path retains items unchanged and creates no ruling. New automatic holds use the same durable posting and failed-post fallback delivered by US-006.

Use makeBotFixEnv and the US-006 outcome fixtures; spentUsd is initially 0 and limitUsd 5. Existing chain rulings are own wrapped comments. Read confirmed keys once with SettlementReadInput formed like fix-carried.ts, including threads/login, top-level own comments, ref/deps/cwd. Read replay/ancestry only from own PR comments, never from the advisor ledger. Two siblings on the same push are each asked unless they actually name each other as a parent. Put these tests in chain-advise-ruled.test.ts to avoid exceeding the test-file limit.

**Scope** — In: composition tests 2, 4, 5, 6, one confirmed-key read, replay, repeated-fix and parent holds, sticky cost limit. Out: settlement parser changes (US-003), decision mapping/post fallback (US-006), fix instruction consumers (US-008), readiness candidate union (US-009). Reading the advisor's decision ledger to find earlier chain rulings: a chain ruling is read only from the pull request's own comments. A second advisor ruling on a ruled chain: a later finding whose lineage parent has a chain ruling is held for a human. Two sibling findings raised in one review round on the same push: each is asked separately, since neither is the other's lineage parent. Detecting that two findings in different rounds are the same finding by their wording: the routing uses the finding key and lineage only.

```ts
// Existing reader consumed through _chainAdviseDeps:
readConfirmedKeys(input: SettlementReadInput): Promise<ReadonlySet<string>>;
```

userStories.title: Keep advisor-held findings in the live readiness hold
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve same-run readiness blocking for held chain findings removed from review.agreed.

**Motivation** — What is missing is a decision point between the review and the fixer.

**Approach** — **A held finding stays open until a writer rules.** The thread is not resolved. Readiness reads its open blocking keys from `review.agreed`, which no longer holds the item, so `openFindingHold` in `fix-report.ts` also takes the keys of `env.chainRulings` entries with outcome `held` (US-009). They go through the same `openKeys` reconciliation as every other key, so a writer's `waive:` on the thread lifts the hold. A ready-only pass does not run the routing and reads the unfiltered artifact, where the held finding is still an open blocking finding. A writer's `confirm` on the thread makes the next `nax bot fix` hand the item to the fixer without asking the advisor; a writer's `waive:` settles it through the existing path.

`packages/nax/src/bot/fix-report.ts`, the private `openFindingHold(env)`.
Baseline: the candidate keys are `blockingKeys(readinessReview(env), blocking)` plus the carried keys.
Target: the candidate keys also include the key of every `env.chainRulings` entry with outcome `held` that is not already among them. All candidates still pass through `openKeys`.

Failure handling: A held finding is absent from `review.agreed` when readiness is decided — Its key is still a candidate open key, from `env.chainRulings`.

Each AC calls readyStep with makeBotFixEnv for a draft PR whose CI is green, with _fixReportDeps stubbed so that no key is settled or confirmed unless the AC says otherwise. Extend existing test/unit/bot/fix-report.test.ts readyStep assertions. Keep existing blocking trigger selection, codeReview/readinessReview preference, carried-key handling, live PR reads and fail-closed reconciliation; held keys join the same deduplicated candidate set, not a new readiness mechanism.

**Scope** — In: held-chain candidate keys in openFindingHold, readyStep behavioral tests, and preservation of the existing no-chainRulings open-finding hold. Out: replay and writer-confirm routing (US-007), filtering and outcome posting (US-006), runBotFix/ready-only wiring (US-008). Surfacing a held finding as a workflow open item: it stays a blocking finding thread. Any change to `BOT_FIX_GRAPH`: no node, exit, transition or `BotFixState` field is added.
